stem: Mr. Allen pairs each student in his class (input) with the month the student was born (output). Which statement is correct?

choices.t: It is a function, because each student has exactly one birth month.
choices.why: Yes. Each input (a student) goes to exactly one output (a month).

choices.t: It is not a function, because two students can share a birth month.
choices.why: Outputs are allowed to repeat. What matters is that each input has only one output.

choices.t: It is not a function, because some months may have no students.
choices.why: A function does not need to use every possible output. Each input just needs exactly one output.

choices.t: It is a function, because each month has exactly one student.
choices.why: You checked the outputs. Many students can share a month — what matters is that each student has one month.

hint: Ask: can one student have two different birth months?
explain: A function gives each input exactly one output.
Input = a student. Output = that student's birth month.
Each student has only one birth month. Sharing a month is fine.
So the relation is a function.

stem: Use the vertical line test. Which graph shows a function?

choices.why: Any vertical line crosses this U-shape at most once, so it is a function.

t.alt: U-shaped curve opening to the right

choices.why: A vertical line such as x = 1 crosses this curve twice, so it is not a function.
A vertical line such as x = 0 crosses the circle twice (top and bottom), so it is not a function.
The vertical line x = 2 touches this graph at every point — infinitely many outputs for one input.

hint: Picture sliding a straight up-and-down line across each graph. Does it ever hit the graph twice?
explain: Vertical line test: if any vertical line touches the graph more than once, it is not a function.
The sideways U and the circle are each hit twice by some vertical line.
The vertical line x = 2 has one input with many outputs.
The U opening up is hit only once by every vertical line, so it is the function.

stem: Let f(x) = −2x + 5. Remember, f(x) is the output (y). Which ordered pair shows where f(x) = −7?

choices.why: You used −7 as the input. f(x) = −7 means −7 is the output, so it goes second.
You added 5 instead of subtracting it. −2x + 5 = −7 gives −2x = −12.

hint: Set −2x + 5 equal to −7 and solve for x.
explain: f(x) = −7 means the output is −7: −2x + 5 = −7.
Subtract 5: −2x = −12.
Divide by −2: x = 6.
The ordered pair is (input, output) = (6, −7).

stem: A water tank is drained. The graph and table show the water left over time. During which time does the water drain fastest, and how fast?

visual.alt: Water drains: flat, down, flat, down

choices.t: 8 to 10 minutes, at 12.5 gallons per minute
choices.why: Yes. 25 gallons drain in 2 minutes: 25 ÷ 2 = 12.5 gallons per minute.

choices.t: 2 to 5 minutes, at 5 gallons per minute
choices.why: 5 gallons per minute is right for 2–5, but 8–10 is steeper: 12.5 gallons per minute.

choices.t: 8 to 10 minutes, at 25 gallons per minute
choices.why: 25 is the total drop. Divide by the 2 minutes it took to get the rate.

choices.t: 2 to 5 minutes, at 15 gallons per minute
choices.why: 15 is the total drop, and it took 3 minutes. That is only 5 gallons per minute.

hint: Find the drop in gallons for each part, then divide by the minutes it took.
explain: 0–2 min and 5–8 min: the line is flat, so the water stays the same.
2–5 min: 40 → 25 is a drop of 15 in 3 min = 5 gallons per minute.
8–10 min: 25 → 0 is a drop of 25 in 2 min = 12.5 gallons per minute.
12.5 > 5, so it drains fastest from 8 to 10 minutes (the steepest part).

stem: Jordan says, “y = x² is a function, so x = y² must be a function too.” Which argument is correct?

choices.t: Jordan is wrong. In x = y², the input x = 4 has two outputs, y = 2 and y = −2.
choices.why: Yes. One input with two outputs means x = y² is not a function.

choices.t: Jordan is right. Both equations use a square, so they work the same way.
choices.why: Where the square is matters. In x = y², one x can pair with a positive and a negative y.

choices.t: Jordan is wrong. In y = x², x = 2 and x = −2 both give y = 4, so neither is a function.
choices.why: Two inputs sharing an output is allowed. y = x² is a function.

choices.t: Jordan is right. In x = y², each y-value gives exactly one x-value.
choices.why: You checked the wrong direction. A function needs each x (input) to have one y.

hint: Try x = 4 in x = y². How many y-values work?
explain: y = x²: each x has one square, so each input has one output — a function.
x = y²: if x = 4, then y² = 4, so y = 2 or y = −2.
One input (4) has two outputs, so x = y² is not a function.
The graph shows it too: x = y² fails the vertical line test.

stem: Movie tickets cost $9 each. A person can buy 0 to 6 tickets. The cost is f(n) = 9n for n tickets, so f(4) = 36. What are the domain and range of f?

choices.why: Yes. You can only buy whole tickets, and each cost is 9 times the number of tickets.

choices.t:
Domain: all numbers from 0 to 6
Range: all numbers from 0 to 54
choices.why: This includes 2.5 tickets. You can't buy part of a ticket, so only whole numbers work.
You swapped them. The domain is the inputs (tickets); the range is the outputs (dollars).
You left out 0. The problem says a person can buy 0 to 6 tickets, so f(0) = 0 counts.

hint: The input n is the number of tickets. Which numbers of tickets make sense?
explain: Inputs are whole numbers of tickets from 0 to 6: domain {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}.
Outputs are f(n) = 9n for each input: 0, 9, 18, 27, 36, 45, 54.
2.5 is not in the domain because you can't buy half a ticket.
f(4) = 9(4) = 36 means 4 tickets cost $36.

There is no number written before x, but −x means −1 · x, so m = −1.
You swapped them. m is the number multiplying x; b is the number added on.

explain: In y = mx + b, m multiplies x and b is added on.
−x is the same as −1x, so m = −1.

stem: Use rise over run to find the slope of the line. Then give the y-intercept.

choices.why: Yes. Up 8 and right 2 is 8 ÷ 2 = 4, and the line crosses the y-axis at −3.
You did run ÷ rise. Slope is rise ÷ run = 8 ÷ 2 = 4.
{{3|4}} is where the line crosses the x-axis. The y-intercept is on the y-axis.
8 is the rise. Divide it by the run, 2, to get the slope.

hint: Count how far up and how far right you move from (0, −3) to (2, 5).
explain: Run = 2 − 0 = 2 (right).
Slope = rise ÷ run = 8 ÷ 2 = 4.
The line crosses the y-axis at (0, −3), so the y-intercept is −3.

stem: Which argument correctly explains why y = 4x + 3 has a constant rate of change?

choices.t: If x goes up by 1, y = 4(x + 1) + 3 = 4x + 7. That is always 4 more than 4x + 3.
choices.why: Yes. This works for every x, so y always grows by 4 per 1 in x.

choices.t: Each time x goes up by 1, the +3 is added again, so y always goes up by 3.
choices.why: The 3 is added only once, to every y. It is the y-intercept, not the rate.

choices.t: When x = 1, y = 7, and 7 ÷ 1 = 7. So y always goes up by 7 for each 1 in x.
choices.why: y ÷ x is not the rate unless b = 0. From x = 1 to x = 2, y goes from 7 to 11: up 4.

choices.t: From x = 0 to x = 1, y goes up by 4. One check like this proves it for any equation.
choices.why: One check is not enough. y = x² also goes up by 1 from 0 to 1, then by 3, then by 5.

hint: Compare y at any x with y at x + 1. What is the difference?
explain: Difference: (4x + 7) − (4x + 3) = 4, for every x.
So y always goes up 4 when x goes up 1 — a constant rate set by m.
The +3 is in every y-value, so it cancels out of the differences.

stem: Which situation can be modeled with a linear function?

choices.t: A taxi charges $3 plus $2 per mile.
choices.why: Yes. The cost goes up by the same $2 every mile — a constant rate.

choices.t: A number of bacteria doubles every hour.
choices.why: Doubling adds more each hour (1, 2, 4, 8…). The change is not constant.

choices.t: The area of a square with side length s.
choices.why: Area = s². Squaring makes the change grow, so it is not linear.

choices.t: A phone loses half of its value every year.
choices.why: Halving takes away a different amount each year. The change is not constant.

hint: Look for a situation that adds or subtracts the same amount each step.
explain: Linear means a constant rate of change: the same amount added each step.
Taxi: +$2 every mile → linear (y = 2x + 3).
Doubling, halving, and squaring change by different amounts → nonlinear.

hint: For P, count from (−2, 6) to (2, −2). For Q and R, ask: which one has rise 0, and which has run 0?
explain: P: from (−2, 6) to (2, −2), rise = −8 (down), run = 4 (right). Slope = −8 ÷ 4 = −2.
Q is horizontal: rise = 0, so slope = 0.
R is vertical: run = 0, and you can't divide by 0, so the slope is undefined.

stem: An elevator starts 80 feet above the ground and goes down 4 feet each second. Which equation gives its height y (feet) after x seconds?

choices.why: Yes. It loses 4 feet per second (m = −4) and starts at 80 feet (b = 80).
The elevator goes down, so the height gets smaller. The slope must be −4.
You swapped them. The rate (−4 per second) multiplies x; the start (80) is added.
This starts at 0 feet. The elevator starts at 80 feet, so b = 80.

hint: Which number is the starting height, and which is the change each second?
explain: The rate of change is −4 feet per second (going down), so m = −4.
The starting height at x = 0 is 80 feet, so b = 80.

stem: Find the slope of the line through (−3, 8) and (5, −4). Kayla wrote (−4 − 8) ÷ (−3 − 5) and got {{3|2}}. Which statement is correct?

choices.t: The slope is −{{3|2}}. Kayla subtracted the x-values in the opposite order from the y-values.
choices.why: Yes. The bottom should be 5 − (−3) = 8, so the slope is −12 ÷ 8 = −{{3|2}}.

choices.t: The slope is {{3|2}}. Kayla's work is correct.
choices.why: The line goes down from left to right, so the slope must be negative.

choices.t: The slope is −{{2|3}}. Kayla should have put the x-values on top.
choices.why: The slope formula is change in y on top, change in x on the bottom.

choices.why: −4 − 8 = −12 is right. Her mistake is on the bottom: −3 − 5 is in the wrong order.

hint: In the slope formula, subtract the y-values and the x-values in the same order.
explain: m = {{y₂ − y₁|x₂ − x₁}}, with (x₁, y₁) = (−3, 8) and (x₂, y₂) = (5, −4).
Kayla used y₂ − y₁ on top but x₁ − x₂ on the bottom, so her sign flipped.

stem: A line passes through (−2, 7) and (4, −2). Which equation in slope-intercept form describes the line?

choices.why: Yes. The slope is −9 ÷ 6 = −{{3|2}}, and both points check.
Sign slip finding b: b = 7 − (−{{3|2}})(−2) = 7 − 3 = 4, not 7 + 3.
The y-values go down as x goes up, so the slope must be negative.
7 is y when x = −2, not when x = 0. Solve for b.

hint: Find the slope first. Then put one point into y = mx + b to find b.

stem: A plumber charges a flat fee plus an hourly rate. A 2-hour job costs $170, and a 5-hour job costs $335. Which equation fits, and how many hours long was a $500 job?

choices.why: Yes. $165 for 3 more hours is $55 per hour, the fee is $60, and 55(8) + 60 = 500.
$170 is the cost of a 2-hour job, not the fee. The fee is the cost at 0 hours.
$165 is the cost for 3 hours. Divide by 3 to get the hourly rate.
Subtract the fee, don't add it: 500 − 60 = 440, and 440 ÷ 55 = 8.

hint: The rate is the change in cost ÷ the change in hours. The fee is the cost at 0 hours.

stem: A car's gas tank has 11.2 gallons after 30 miles and 8.5 gallons after 120 miles. Gas use is linear. Which model gives the gallons y left after x miles, and how much gas is left after 250 miles?

11.2 gallons is the amount at 30 miles, not at 0 miles. Work back to find b.

hint: Find the rate in gallons per mile, then work back to 0 miles to find the starting amount.
explain: b = 11.2 − (−0.03)(30) = 11.2 + 0.9 = 12.1 gallons (the full tank at 0 miles).

stem: Two savings plans are shown. If both patterns continue, which statement is correct?

choices.t: Plan A is linear (+$10 each week). Plan B is not (it doubles). Plan B first has more in week 7.
choices.why: Yes. In week 6, A = $80 and B = $64. In week 7, A = $90 and B = $128.

choices.t: Both plans are linear because both go up every week. Plan B never has more than Plan A.
choices.why: Going up is not enough. Plan B goes up by $1, $2, $4, $8… — not a constant amount.

choices.t: Plan A is linear (+$10 each week). Plan B is not (it doubles). Plan B never passes Plan A.
